author: Anttipatia
quote:
I don't know what to say. I started playing last Friday and I’ve already racked up over 30 hours, which should tell you everything about how hooked I am. This is one of those rare games that just lets you exist in its world and do whatever you want, without constantly pulling you back onto a strict path. 

Visually, the game is absolutely stunning. Every environment feels handcrafted, alive, and worth exploring. I’ve caught myself multiple times just stopping to explore for new things, which doesn’t happen often in modern AAA games. The world isn’t just big, it feels filled and meaningful. 

The combat is easily a 10/10. It’s fluid, impactful, and satisfying in a way that makes every encounter feel engaging while difficult at the same time. It never really gets old. There’s a weight to it that a lot of games try to achieve but don’t quite land.

What I really don’t understand is the hate this game got early on. It feels like it’s being criticized for the same systems that other games have been praised for. The difference is, Crimson Desert actually executes them better. Yet somehow, when this game does it, it becomes a problem? Sure, no game is perfect, but the level of criticism this received just doesn’t match the experience I’m having. 

If anything, it feels like people made up their minds before giving it a real chance. For me, this has been one of the most immersive and enjoyable experiences in a long time. If you’re on the fence, I’d say it’s absolutely worth diving into.
